properties.name: Increment 3 of the absorption — the graph algorithms come in-tree, and this is the first increment carrying real intellectual content
properties.rationale:
This is the first increment where the plan's own warning applies. Increments 1 and 2 were self-contained arithmetic with no external crates and one or two call sites; this carries a Leiden community-detection implementation, a DFS lowlink cut walk, and Tarjan SCC — the code you would least want to reimplement, which under ABSORPTION inverts into the argument FOR: difficulty-to-rewrite stops being a cost and becomes the reason the code is worth owning.

⭐ THE CLOSURE WAS COMPUTED, NOT ESTIMATED, and the method matters because the first attempt at it was wrong. An earlier pass grepped `crate::[a-z_]+` and missed `use crate::{a, b}` forms, and separately truncated the crate's file list at 12 — so it reported 7 unneeded files when there are 11, and 3,832 lines split differently. Re-run over every file with both import shapes, the split is 1,844 needed / 1,988 dropped. **A closure measured with a pattern that cannot see one of the two syntaxes is not a closure.**

🛑 THE CONDITION FROM `dec:absorbed-code-is-distributed-by-function` APPLIES HERE FOR THE FIRST TIME: absorbing behaviour that was modelled as a `required` interface deletes the framing that explained why reflow2 had no requirement for it. `ifc:req-dyno-graph-api` says "reflow2 NEEDS graph algorithms from outside"; once they are in-tree, nothing says why reflow2 detects communities with Leiden. Anthony stated the reason himself on 2026-08-17 — *"I wanted graph theory to undergird everything ... graph theory was important to my concept of reflow2"* — and it has never been written as a requirement. It is captured now, at `proposed`, because a requirement is his word and not session residue.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
Third increment of `dec:absorb-the-foundation-subset-and-end-the-dependency`. The closure behind the six names reflow2 imports — `GraphBuilder`, `leiden`, `strongly_connected_components`, `connected_components`, `find_cycle`, `cut_structure` — is absorbed from `dynograph-graph` at tag v0.12.0 into a new `reflow2-core` module, with its tests. `allocate.rs`, `flow.rs` and `structure.rs` import locally, and `dynograph-graph` is removed from reflow2's dependencies.

TAKEN, 1,844 lines in 8 files, verified as the transitive closure rather than guessed: `error.rs` (62), `graph.rs` (334), `components.rs` (134), `scc.rs` (169), `cycles.rs` (154), `cuts.rs` (223), `communities.rs` (695), `lib.rs` (73).

NOT TAKEN, 1,988 lines in 11 files — **51% of the crate**: betweenness, centrality, closeness, clustering, eigenvector, link_prediction, maxflow, pagerank, paths, shortest_path, toposort. reflow2 calls none of them.

⭐ `cuts.rs` DOES NOT NEED `maxflow.rs`, which is the one result worth checking rather than assuming: articulation points and bridges are computed by a DFS lowlink walk, not by a min-cut, so `max_flow_min_cut` (248 lines) stays behind. A closure taken on the intuition that "cuts need flow" would have dragged it in.

The absorbed code lands in a NEW component `cmp:graph-algorithms`, under `sys:foundation` — Anthony's name, chosen because reflow2 already has a `cmp:graph` for its own graph module and the two are different things. That collision was found before the code moved, not during.
